3:     panic::{RefUnwindSafe, UnwindSafe},

9:     regex_automata::{

11:         PatternID,

16: use crate::{

18:     error::Error,
19:     matcher::RegexCaptures,
20:     non_matching::non_matching_bytes,
21:     strip::strip_from_match,

24: type PoolFn =
25:     Box<dyn Fn() -> Captures + Send + Sync + UnwindSafe + RefUnwindSafe>;
26: 
27: /// A matcher for implementing "word match" semantics.
28: #[derive(Debug)]
29: pub(crate) struct WordMatcher {
30:     /// The regex which is roughly `(?:^|\W)(<original pattern>)(?:$|\W)`.
31:     regex: Regex,
32:     /// The HIR that produced the regex above. We don't keep the HIR for the
33:     /// `original` regex.
34:     ///
35:     /// We put this in an `Arc` because by the time it gets here, it won't
36:     /// change. And because cloning and dropping an `Hir` is somewhat expensive
37:     /// due to its deep recursive representation.
38:     chir: Arc<ConfiguredHIR>,
39:     /// The original regex supplied by the user, which we use in a fast path
40:     /// to try and detect matches before deferring to slower engines.
41:     original: Regex,
42:     /// A map from capture group name to capture group index.
43:     names: HashMap<String, usize>,
44:     /// A thread-safe pool of reusable buffers for finding the match offset of
45:     /// the inner group.
46:     caps: Arc<Pool<Captures, PoolFn>>,
47: }
48: 
49: impl Clone for WordMatcher {
50:     fn clone(&self) -> WordMatcher {
51:         // We implement Clone manually so that we get a fresh Pool such that it
52:         // can set its own thread owner. This permits each thread usings `caps`
53:         // to hit the fast path.
54:         //
55:         // Note that cloning a regex is "cheap" since it uses reference
56:         // counting internally.
57:         let re = self.regex.clone();
58:         WordMatcher {
59:             regex: self.regex.clone(),
60:             chir: Arc::clone(&self.chir),
61:             original: self.original.clone(),
62:             names: self.names.clone(),
63:             caps: Arc::new(Pool::new(Box::new(move || re.create_captures()))),
64:         }
65:     }
66: }
67: 
68: impl WordMatcher {
69:     /// Create a new matcher from the given pattern that only produces matches
70:     /// that are considered "words."
71:     ///
72:     /// The given options are used to construct the regular expression
73:     /// internally.
74:     pub(crate) fn new(chir: ConfiguredHIR) -> Result<WordMatcher, Error> {
75:         let original = chir.clone().into_anchored().to_regex()?;
76:         let chir = Arc::new(chir.into_word()?);
77:         let regex = chir.to_regex()?;
78:         let caps = Arc::new(Pool::new({
79:             let regex = regex.clone();
80:             Box::new(move || regex.create_captures()) as PoolFn
81:         }));
82: 
83:         let mut names = HashMap::new();
84:         let it = regex.group_info().pattern_names(PatternID::ZERO);
85:         for (i, optional_name) in it.enumerate() {
86:             if let Some(name) = optional_name {
87:                 names.insert(name.to_string(), i.checked_sub(1).unwrap());
88:             }
89:         }
90:         Ok(WordMatcher { regex, chir, original, names, caps })
91:     }
92: 
93:     /// Return the underlying regex used to match at word boundaries.
94:     ///
95:     /// The original regex is in the capture group at index 1.
96:     pub(crate) fn regex(&self) -> &Regex {
97:         &self.regex
98:     }
99: 
100:     /// Return the underlying HIR for the regex used to match at word
101:     /// boundaries.
102:     pub(crate) fn chir(&self) -> &ConfiguredHIR {
103:         &self.chir
104:     }
105: 
106:     /// Attempt to do a fast confirmation of a word match that covers a subset
107:     /// (but hopefully a big subset) of most cases. Ok(Some(..)) is returned
108:     /// when a match is found. Ok(None) is returned when there is definitively
109:     /// no match. Err(()) is returned when this routine could not detect
110:     /// whether there was a match or not.
111:     fn fast_find(
112:         &self,
113:         haystack: &[u8],
114:         at: usize,
115:     ) -> Result<Option<Match>, ()> {
116:         // This is a bit hairy. The whole point here is to avoid running a
117:         // slower regex engine to extract capture groups. Remember, our word
118:         // regex looks like this:
119:         //
120:         //     (^|\W)(<original regex>)(\W|$)
121:         //
122:         // What we want are the match offsets of <original regex>. So in the
123:         // easy/common case, the original regex will be sandwiched between
124:         // two codepoints that are in the \W class. So our approach here is to
125:         // look for a match of the overall word regexp, strip the \W ends and
126:         // then check whether the original regex matches what's left. If so,
127:         // then we are guaranteed a correct match.
128:         //
129:         // This only works though if we know that the match is sandwiched
130:         // between two \W codepoints. This only occurs when neither ^ nor $
131:         // match. This in turn only occurs when the match is at either the
132:         // beginning or end of the haystack. In either of those cases, we
133:         // declare defeat and defer to the slower implementation.
134:         //
135:         // The reason why we cannot handle the ^/$ cases here is because we
136:         // can't assume anything about the original pattern. (Try commenting
137:         // out the checks for ^/$ below and run the tests to see examples.)
138:         let config = self.chir.config();
139:         let configured_term = config.line_terminator;
140:         let search_term = self.chir.line_terminator();
141:         let non_matching = non_matching_bytes(self.chir.hir());
142:         let input = Input::new(haystack).span(at..haystack.len());
143:         match self.regex.find(input) {
144:             None => Ok(None),
145:             Some(m) => {
146:                 let cand = Match::new(m.start(), m.end());
147:                 let haystack_len = haystack.len();
148:                 let at_start = cand.start() == 0;
149:                 let at_end = cand.end() == haystack_len;
150:                 if at_start || at_end {
151:                     return Err(());
152:                 }
153:                 let slice = &haystack[cand];
154:                 let cand_len = cand.len();
155:                 let cand_empty = cand.is_empty();
156:                 let (prefix_ch, slen) = if cand_empty || slice.is_empty() {
157:                     (None, 0)
158:                 } else if slice[0] <= 0x7F {
159:                     (Some(slice[0] as char), 1)
160:                 } else {
161:                     bstr::decode_utf8(slice)
162:                 };
163:                 let (suffix_ch, elen) = if cand_empty || slice.is_empty() {
164:                     (None, 0)
165:                 } else if slice[cand_len - 1] <= 0x7F {
166:                     (Some(slice[cand_len - 1] as char), 1)
167:                 } else {
168:                     let mut start = cand_len - 1;
169:                     let limit = cand_len.saturating_sub(4);
170:                     while start > limit && slice[start] & 0xC0 == 0x80
171:                     {
172:                         start -= 1;
173:                     }
174:                     let tail = &slice[start..];
175:                     let (ch, size) = bstr::decode_utf8(tail);
176:                     if start + size != cand_len {
177:                         (None, 1)
178:                     } else {
179:                         (ch, size)
180:                     }
181:                 };
182:                 let slen = match prefix_ch {
183:                     Some(ch) => ch.len_utf8(),
184:                     None => slen,
185:                 };
186:                 let elen = match suffix_ch {
187:                     Some(ch) => ch.len_utf8(),
188:                     None => elen,
189:                 };
190:                 let new_start = cand.start() + slen;
191:                 let new_end = cand.end() - elen;
192:                 if new_start > new_end {
193:                     return Err(());
194:                 }
195:                 if new_start > haystack_len || new_end > haystack_len {
196:                     return Err(());
197:                 }
198:                 let inner_match = Match::new(new_start, new_end);
199:                 let inner = &haystack[inner_match];
200:                 let inner_len = inner_match.len();
201:                 let mut inner_impossible = inner_len > 0;
202:                 let mut i = 0;
203:                 while i < inner_len {
204:                     let b = inner[i];
205:                     if !non_matching.contains(b) {
206:                         inner_impossible = false;
207:                         break;
208:                     }
209:                     i += 1;
210:                 }
211:                 let term = if let Some(t) = search_term {
212:                     Some(t)
213:                 } else {
214:                     configured_term
215:                 };
216:                 let mut blocked = inner_impossible;
217:                 if let Some(term) = term {
218:                     if inner_len > 0 {
219:                         if term.is_crlf() || config.crlf {
220:                             let mut j = 0;
221:                             while j < inner_len {
222:                                 let b = inner[j];
223:                                 if b == b'\r' || b == b'\n' {
224:                                     blocked = true;
225:                                     break;
226:                                 }
227:                                 j += 1;
228:                             }
229:                         } else {
230:                             let t = term.as_byte();
231:                             let mut j = 0;
232:                             while j < inner_len {
233:                                 if inner[j] == t {
234:                                     blocked = true;
235:                                     break;
236:                                 }
237:                                 j += 1;
238:                             }
239:                         }
240:                         if !blocked {
241:                             if let Err(_) = strip_from_match(
242:                                 Hir::literal(inner.to_vec()),
243:                                 term,
244:                             ) {
245:                                 blocked = true;
246:                             }
247:                         }
248:                     }
249:                 }
250:                 if blocked {
251:                     Err(())
252:                 } else if self.original.is_match(inner) {
253:                     Ok(Some(inner_match))
254:                 } else {
255:                     Err(())
256:                 }
257:             }
258:         }
259:     }
260: }

271:         // To make this easy to get right, we extract captures here instead of

273:         // of `0`. We *could* use `find_at` here and then trim the match after
274:         // the fact, but that's a bit harder to get right, and it's not clear
275:         // if it's worth it.

279:         // a slower regex engine to extract capture groups in the vast majority
280:         // of cases. However, the slower engine is I believe required for full
281:         // correctness.
282:         match self.fast_find(haystack, at) {
283:             Ok(Some(m)) => return Ok(Some(m)),

145: /// produced this HIR.
146: ///
147: /// Since the configuration is tracked, values with this type can be
148: /// transformed into other HIR expressions (or regular expressions) in a way
149: /// that preserves the configuration. For example, the `fast_line_regex`
150: /// method will apply literal extraction to the inner HIR and use that to build
151: /// a new regex that matches the extracted literals in a way that is
152: /// consistent with the configuration that produced this HIR. For example, the
153: /// size limits set on the configured HIR will be propagated out to any
154: /// subsequently constructed HIR or regular expression.
155: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
156: pub(crate) struct ConfiguredHIR {
157:     config: Config,
158:     hir: Hir,
159: }
160: 
161: impl ConfiguredHIR {
162:     /// Parse the given patterns into a single HIR expression that represents
163:     /// an alternation of the patterns given.
164:     fn new<P: AsRef<str>>(
165:         config: Config,
166:         patterns: &[P],
167:     ) -> Result<ConfiguredHIR, Error> {
168:         let hir = if config.is_fixed_strings(patterns) {
169:             let mut alts = vec![];
170:             for p in patterns.iter() {
171:                 alts.push(Hir::literal(p.as_ref().as_bytes()));
172:             }
173:             log::debug!(
174:                 "assembling HIR from {} fixed string literals",
175:                 alts.len()
176:             );
177:             let hir = Hir::alternation(alts);
178:             hir
179:         } else {
180:             let mut alts = vec![];
181:             for p in patterns.iter() {
182:                 alts.push(if config.fixed_strings {
183:                     format!("(?:{})", regex_syntax::escape(p.as_ref()))
184:                 } else {
185:                     format!("(?:{})", p.as_ref())
186:                 });
187:             }
188:             let pattern = alts.join("|");
189:             let ast = ast::parse::ParserBuilder::new()
190:                 .nest_limit(config.nest_limit)
191:                 .octal(config.octal)
192:                 .ignore_whitespace(config.ignore_whitespace)
193:                 .build()
194:                 .parse(&pattern)
195:                 .map_err(Error::generic)?;
196:             let analysis = AstAnalysis::from_ast(&ast);
197:             let mut hir = hir::translate::TranslatorBuilder::new()
198:                 .utf8(false)
199:                 .case_insensitive(config.is_case_insensitive(&analysis))
200:                 .multi_line(config.multi_line)
201:                 .dot_matches_new_line(config.dot_matches_new_line)
202:                 .crlf(config.crlf)
203:                 .swap_greed(config.swap_greed)
204:                 .unicode(config.unicode)
205:                 .build()
206:                 .translate(&pattern, &ast)
207:                 .map_err(Error::generic)?;
208:             // We don't need to do this for the fixed-strings case above
209:             // because is_fixed_strings will return false if any pattern
210:             // contains a line terminator. Therefore, we don't need to strip
211:             // it.
212:             //
213:             // We go to some pains to avoid doing this in the fixed-strings
214:             // case because this can result in building a new HIR when ripgrep
215:             // is given a huge set of literals to search for. And this can
216:             // actually take a little time. It's not huge, but it's noticeable.
217:             hir = match config.line_terminator {
218:                 None => hir,
219:                 Some(line_term) => strip_from_match(hir, line_term)?,
220:             };
221:             hir
222:         };
223:         Ok(ConfiguredHIR { config, hir })
224:     }

226:     /// Return a reference to the underlying configuration.
227:     pub(crate) fn config(&self) -> &Config {
228:         &self.config
229:     }
230: 
231:     /// Return a reference to the underyling HIR.
232:     pub(crate) fn hir(&self) -> &Hir {
233:         &self.hir
234:     }
235: 
236:     /// Convert this HIR to a regex that can be used for matching.
237:     pub(crate) fn to_regex(&self) -> Result<Regex, Error> {
238:         let meta = Regex::config()
239:             .utf8_empty(false)
240:             .nfa_size_limit(Some(self.config.size_limit))
241:             // We don't expose a knob for this because the one-pass DFA is
242:             // usually not a perf bottleneck for ripgrep. But we give it some
243:             // extra room than the default.
244:             .onepass_size_limit(Some(10 * (1 << 20)))
245:             // Same deal here. The default limit for full DFAs is VERY small,
246:             // but with ripgrep we can afford to spend a bit more time on
247:             // building them I think.
248:             .dfa_size_limit(Some(1 * (1 << 20)))
